_comment: Canonical Sesame Sync signing payloads, generated by Go's
syncproto.Envelope.signingPayload, which is what the service verifies.
Both implementations assert against this file rather than against each
src-tauri/src/sync/envelope.rs. If they only compared to themselves, the
two could drift together and every signature would still look valid on
each side while failing across the boundary.
The exact bytes matter. Go's json.Marshal emits fields in struct order,
compact, and omits tombstoneId when empty. Changing field order, spacing,
or omitempty here silently invalidates every signature a desktop produces.
The tombstone operation was removed; only snapshots exist.
_rustSignedComment: A snapshot envelope signed by the Rust client in src-tauri/src/sync/envelope.rs,
using the fictional deterministic signing key [7u8; 32].
backend/internal/syncproto verifies this with the same VerifySignature the
service uses. Matching signing payloads prove the two encoders agree; this
proves a signature actually crosses the boundary, which is the property that
matters and the one a payload comparison alone can miss.
